subject: Capture output from programs/tools run within knitr

messages.author: 6c3216148f5b74fa
messages.subject: Capture output from programs/tools run within knitr
parts:
Hi,

I am running a perl script within knitr.   The perl script in turn calls an external program that generates an output to the console when done running.  I would like to capture that output in the text file that is generated by knitr.  Could someone help me with information on how I could do so.

Thanks,

- Pankaj

Pankaj Agarwal
Bioinformatician
Duke Bioinformatics Shared Resource
Duke Cancer Institute
Duke University

messages.author: 6c3216148f5b74fa
messages.subject: Re: Capture output from programs/tools run within knitr
parts:
The perl code in my knitr/R script that runs the external tool called bowtie2:

...
....
...
```{r test-perl, engine='perl'}
use strict;
use warnings;
use Cwd qw(cwd);
my $cur_dir = cwd;
print " Current working dir: [$cur_dir] ";
my $bowtie2_exe = '/data/installs/bowtie2/bowtie2-2.2.1/bowtie2';
...
...
my $cmd="$bowtie2_exe -x $bowtie2_index -1 $fastq_file_pe_1 -2 $fastq_file_pe_2 -S $cur_dir/"."$fastq_files[$cnt]".".sam -p 8";
print " command is [$cmd] ";
system($cmd);
...
...

The variables are populated earlier in the code.  The translated command as reported in the knitr report text file is:

## command is [/data/installs/bowtie2/bowtie2-2.2.1/bowtie2 -x /data/ref_genomes/human/37.2/Homo_sapiens/NCBI/build37.2/Sequence/Bowtie2Index/genome -1 /data/projects/knitr/xxxx_1.clipped.fastq.gz -2 /data/projects/knitr/xxxx_2.clipped.fastq.gz -S /data/projects/knitr/xxxx.sam -p 8]

When the command is done running, the output from the command is printed out in the R console:

53545457 reads; of these:
  53545457 (100.00%) were paired; of these:
    6637517 (12.40%) aligned concordantly 0 times
...
...

But this is not captured in the knitr report text file.

Ideally it is important to capture this because a change in the parameters to the bowtie2 command will generate a different output, which should be captured in the report.  Otherwise I would have to copy and paste it in the report.

Please let me know if you need further information.

Thanks,

- Pankaj

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Capture output from programs/tools run within knitr
parts:
As I said, I'm not an expert on Perl, neither do I know bowtie2. What
I can do is to test some standard system commands, e.g. this works
pretty well for me:

```{r engine='perl'}
system("ls");
system("echo foo bar");
```

So the problem might be from bowtie2. Does it write to stdout?

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.author: 6c3216148f5b74fa
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: Capture output from programs/tools run within knitr
parts:
It turned out that bowtie2 was writing to stderr, which I guess is not captured in knitr.  I redirected to stdout by adding " 2>&1" at the end of the command, and it worked!  The console output was captured by the knitr report.
Thanks for your suggestion and help!
Sincrerely,
- Pankaj
